name: Bright Heart Health
one_liner: Video-based treatment for eating disorders (intensive outpatient and outpatient) and for opioid use with buprenorphine; takes insurance.
best_for: People with an eating disorder who need more than weekly therapy but not residential care
Adults with opioid use disorder who want buprenorphine by video
People without a local eating disorder specialist
People with Medicare or Medicaid in a state where it is accepted
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose: call 911, or call or text 988
People who are medically unstable from an eating disorder and need inpatient or residential care
People outside the states it serves
short_description: Video-based eating disorder programs (IOP and outpatient) and buprenorphine treatment for opioid use; insurance, Medicare, some Medicaid or sliding scale.
long_description: Bright Heart Health is a California-based telehealth provider (headquartered in Walnut Creek) that delivers addiction, eating disorder, mental health and chronic pain programs by video. Its eating disorder program, which it says was the first telemedicine eating disorder program accredited by the Joint Commission, offers intensive outpatient (about 11 hours a week), outpatient and support groups for anorexia, bulimia, binge eating and other eating disorders. Its opioid program prescribes buprenorphine (Suboxone), with physician visits every one to two weeks and video counseling. Its pages say it accepts most major insurance, Medicare and Medicaid in some states (such as California and North Carolina), and offers a sliding scale for self-pay; medication costs are separate. State pages exist for California and North Carolina and a New York telepractice clinic is listed; current states per program were not confirmed. The company has described a preliminary study with a Stanford researcher, but no published study of its programs was found.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; sliding-scale self-pay (price not published)
pricing.notes: Free initial consultation. Accepts most major insurance, Medicare and some state Medicaid (e.g., California, North Carolina). Self-pay fees don't include prescriptions.

privacy.notes: Says it doesn't sell personal data for money, but its opt-out page says third-party cookies may count as a 'sale' or 'sharing' under California law, with an opt-out. Patient records are covered by its HIPAA notice.

seo.meta_description: Bright Heart Health provides virtual eating disorder treatment with medical monitoring, therapy, and nutrition counseling for all eating disorder types.

faqs.q: What eating disorders does Bright Heart Health treat?
faqs.a: Bright Heart treats anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, ARFID (avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder), OSFED, and other eating disorders. They work with adolescents and adults. Medical monitoring is included for conditions requiring it.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover Bright Heart Health?
faqs.a: Yes, Bright Heart accepts many major insurance plans for eating disorder treatment. Coverage varies by plan and state. Contact them to verify your specific insurance benefits before starting treatment.

faqs.q: How is virtual eating disorder treatment delivered?
faqs.a: You meet regularly via video with your treatment team: a physician for medical monitoring, therapist for individual/family therapy, psychiatrist for medication if needed, and dietitian for nutrition counseling. The team coordinates care together rather than working in silos.

faqs.q: Is virtual treatment effective for eating disorders?
faqs.a: Research shows telehealth eating disorder treatment can be effective, especially for outpatient-level care. Bright Heart's multidisciplinary approach mirrors what's offered in specialized clinics. For severe cases requiring intensive medical monitoring, higher levels of care may be needed.

primary_uses: Virtual intensive outpatient care for eating disorders
Outpatient therapy and support groups for eating disorders
Buprenorphine (Suboxone) treatment for opioid use disorder

patient_summary: You start with a free consultation, and Bright Heart checks your insurance; care then happens by video on your phone or computer. For eating disorders there are intensive outpatient (about 11 hours a week), outpatient and support-group levels; for opioid use you see a physician weekly or every two weeks for buprenorphine (Suboxone) plus counseling. It takes many insurance plans, Medicare and some Medicaid, with a sliding scale for self-pay.

availability.note: Only in some states (state pages for CA and NC; NY telepractice clinic listed); current states for each program not confirmed.
